attempts.label: DANDI:001950
attempts.entry_title: LC-NE activity during dynamic foraging (Su et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's behavioural and response findings on locus coeruleus norepinephrine (LC-NE) neurons largely held up here, but its maps of activity within LC mostly did not. Mice used reward history, nearly all neurons were excited by the go cue, baseline firing was higher before ignored cues, and reward-excited neurons and prelimbic LC-NE axons tracked reward prediction error. Ignore- and switch-related activity did not lie ventral and dorsal as reported; the dataset does not mark the paper's neurons, so the selection was rebuilt (252 units against 241). Reward- and no-reward-excited neurons lacked opposing links to later choices. The anatomy and transcriptomics of Figures 1 to 3 and the cortex-projecting neurons could not be tested, as the dataset holds neither.
attempts.description: Tests the behavioral and physiological findings of Su et al. (2026) on dandiset 001950, which holds the dynamic foraging behavior, tetrode and Neuropixels recordings of opto-tagged locus coeruleus neurons, pupil diameter, and fiber photometry of LC-NE axons. It selects the LC-NE units with the criteria of the paper's code, tests the choice and engagement regressions, go-cue, engagement, switch and outcome coding of single neurons and of axons in prelimbic cortex, their relation to position in LC, and the pupil and lick analyses. The anatomy, transcriptomics and slice findings are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.notes: Re-run after a reader's answer (questions/001950.yaml), which amended the criterion. A trial is now a go cue with a choice, counted as the code counts session_len for Figure S12a (makeSessionDF with cut_interruptions=True, the longest stretch of choice trials without manual or extra water), and the session sets are (a) the sessions passing beh_only.json, (b) the sessions of the recorded neurons and (c) all sessions. Under reading (b) the 112 sessions of the selected units average 334.3 trials with a range of 94 to 558, the paper's range exactly and the mean within 342 +- 34.2. Reading (a), with the three computable criteria, gives 372 sessions averaging 393.0 (52 to 851), and reading (c) 383 sessions averaging 389.8 (4 to 851), both outside; so do the variants of (a) with the refitted model's aN and bias criteria (261 sessions, 39 mice, 387.1, 74 to 804; the code has 259 sessions and 32 mice) and with the 90-trial bound on the cut count (368 sessions, 396.4, 94 to 851). For reading (b) the count without the cut gives 360.6 (128 to 558) and all go cues 380.3 (176 to 586). Before the answer the claim was not reproduced, with a trial counted as a go cue, and under that count no reading had its mean within tolerance (reading (b), then called (a), 380.3). The table's auto_manual_trial and extra_reward columns agree in every row with their recomputation from the reward deliveries, as get_session_tbl derives them. The version of record gives the range as 94 to 800 (Extended Data Fig. 9); the claims file follows the preprint's 94 to 558, which reading (b) matches.
deviations: The session set of reading (b) is this attempt's 112 sessions, not the code's 106 (see the unit selection); reading (a) applies the three computable criteria of beh_only.json (session_len, p_sw_L, diff_1), with the model-based aN and bias shown as a variant from the per-session refit.
With a model name, makeSessionDF first trims each session to the model's session_cut from the code's session curation table, which is not in the dandiset; no such trim is applied here.
The code keeps rows with animal_response != 2 over the whole trial table; no-go cues are left out here as the criterion says. No no-go cue in the dandiset has a response, so the counts are the same.

outcomes.statement: Inter-trial intervals averaged 4.83 s (range 1.1 to 20 s).
outcomes.source: Methods, Behavioral task, paragraph 6

outcomes.notes: Under the four readings (trial end fixed at 3.0 s for photometry and 3.1 s otherwise, or the table's stop_time; no-go cues ending an interval or not) the mean is 4.43 to 4.96 s, within 4.83 +- 0.483. The range is not within 0.99 to 22 s under any reading; the maximum is 292 s (pauses in a session), 0.72% of intervals exceed 20 s, the shortest is 0.22 s (behavior-only sessions), and the 1st to 99th percentiles are 1.10 to 16.1 s. outcomes.statement: Mice used reward and choice history to guide choices; a logistic regression of choice on outcome history has R2 = 0.60 and predicts 0.88 of choices, with coefficients decaying over past trials (exponential fit coefficient 3.95).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial variation of LC-NE activity, paragraph 3; Figure 4c legend
outcomes.quote: Logistic regression coefficients for choice as a function of outcome history for all mice (error bars are smaller than points). R 2 = 0.60, successful choice prediction, 0.88 ... exponential fit (coefficient of 3.95)
outcomes.notes: Pooled over 39 to 41 mice and 149,081 to 152,905 choices, McFadden R2 = 0.600 to 0.601 and 0.895 of choices predicted under 5, 10 and 15 lags and both models (squared correlation 0.68). Rewarded coefficients decay over lags; all are positive in the R + N model, and in the code's R + C model lags 1 to 4 are positive and lag 5 is -0.025. Per-mouse fits give R2 0.66 to 0.67 and 0.92 predicted. The criterion does not test the exponential fit coefficient, so it does not decide the outcome. Read as the claims file reads it, the decay constant in trials, it does not hold: tau = 1.391 for R + N pooled over 10 lags (the measured value) and 1.23 to 2.28 in every fit, against 3.95 +- 0.395. The amplitude of the same fit is 4.33 (4.28 over 15 lags, 4.55 over 5), within tolerance; R + C gives 2.7 to 2.9. Whether the legend's coefficient is the amplitude is asked of a reader (questions/001950.yaml).
deviations: The rewarded, unrewarded and choice histories the criterion lists are collinear (R + N = C); the code's Figure 4c model (R + C, choice_reward_choice in F_behavior_w_FP.ipynb) and the Methods' R + N are fitted. The measured values are from R + N pooled over 10 lags, the reading that matches all three numbers.
The exponential fit follows _fit_exp_offset of F_behavior_w_FP.ipynb (A exp(-lag/tau) + C, weighted by the SEs).

outcomes.statement: Changes of choice on consecutive trials correlate with the model's RPE (rank correlation rho = 0.84).

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), 8 equal-width RPE bins per session averaged over sessions, rho = 0.833 over all 382 sessions and over the 136 photometry sessions (within 0.84 +- 0.084); 9 bins give 0.917 and 0.867. outcomes.notes: 210 Neuropixels units with CCF under waveform_all.json (16 mice). outcomes.statement: LC-NE spiking correlates with pupil size; pupil autocorrelation decays with a time constant of 3.37 +/- 1.03 s across sessions.
outcomes.source: Figure S16 title and panels i, j; Methods, Pupil auto-correlogram
outcomes.quote: τ had a mean of 3.37 and SD of 1.03
outcomes.notes: Pupil autocorrelation time constant over 133 sessions 3.28 s (SD 1.01) in 0.5 s bins and 3.21 s in 0.1 s bins, within 3.37 +- 1.03. The code's procedure (pupil_analysis.py and F_pupil_beh_ephys.ipynb at 971c1ca: 0.5 s bins, lags to 20 s, the autocorrelogram rescaled by its last value, bounded fit) gives 3.08 s per session (SD 0.96) and 3.46 s weighted by the selected units, as the code averages over unit rows. findings.statement: The published version 0.260928.2230 does not mark which units are the paper's LC-NE neurons or which are cortex-projecting, and holds no per-unit stable recording windows; the Neuropixels files hold all 14,126 sorted units. The draft (modified 2026-10-06) adds opto_NE_paper, antidromic_tier_1, antidromic_tier_2, antidromic_jitter, antidromic_latency, p_antidromic, p_collision, ephys_cut_start, ephys_cut_end and firing_rate_stability to the units tables; publishing it would make the selection and the cortex-projecting claims testable.

Reconstructing the selection from the code's criteria files gives 252 units from 21 mice and 112 sessions, against 241 units and 19 mice; the code's model-based session criteria (aN, bias), its drift cuts and its 0.2 ISI bound for cortex-projecting units need data the published version lacks. The draft's opto_NE_paper marks 267 units and agrees with this selection under the same criteria on 223.
The per-trial spike amplitudes used as a drift regressor in every spike-rate regression, and the Q-learning model's per-trial variables (chosen value, RPE) and parameters, are not in the dandiset.

The anatomy, transcriptomics, MERFISH, retrograde tracing and patch-seq data of Figures 1 to 3 and S1 to S11 are not in the dandiset, which its title and description match; the paper points to a Code Ocean collection without a DOI or other pinned identifier.
Numeric unit columns are stored as strings in some files, isi_violations_ratio in 4 files and peak_to_valley in 54 (for example sub-751004 session 2024-12-23).

Tetrode units lack the quality columns of the Neuropixels files (isi_violations_ratio among them, which the selection needs; it is recomputed here from the spike times, matching the Neuropixels column at r = 0.9993), and have no CCF coordinates. The pupil_diameter series states no unit.
The description of acquisition/right_lick_time reads "The time of left licks".
Two files of subject 763360 (kind ecephys) have no trial table, so they cannot be used in task analyses; the archive counts 42 subjects of which 41 have task data.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Is the exponential fit coefficient of 3.95 (Figure 4c legend) the amplitude or the decay constant, and which choice model and number of lags does it come from? Here the amplitude of the R + N model over 10 or 15 lags matches and no decay constant does. (2) How is the axonal quality threshold of 0.5 z applied (which window, mean or peak)? (3) Figure S15q: is the lick train gap 0.5 s (Methods) or 0.8 s (the load_licks default), and are video or sensor licks used? (4) In Figure S15f, what sign convention do the respond-versus-ignore t-statistics have? Here the correlation with tonic modulation is +0.26, the paper's -0.59. (5) How are the bootstrapped p-values of Figure S15t computed, and how is a pair of neurons placed on a spatial axis? The absences hold here only with a within-session null.

The Methods give a 0.5 s inter-lick interval for lick bouts (Lick bout detection), while load_licks in utils/lick_utils.py (971c1ca), which F_spont_choice_lick_neuron.ipynb calls without arguments, splits trains at 0.8 s. The pupil time constant "mean of 3.37 and SD of 1.03" is computed in F_pupil_beh_ephys.ipynb over unit rows, each session's value repeated for each of its units, not over sessions.

The antidromic stimulation tables the code reads to identify cortex-projecting neurons ({session}_opto_session.csv) and the pupil edge confidence are not in the dandiset, and the trial table's ITI_duration column does not hold the generated inter-trial intervals the Methods describe (it is 0.5 s in every photometry trial).

entries.title: LC-NE activity during dynamic foraging (Su et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the behavioral and physiological findings of Su et al. (2026) on dandiset 001950, which holds the dynamic foraging behavior, tetrode and Neuropixels recordings of opto-tagged locus coeruleus neurons, pupil diameter, and fiber photometry of LC-NE axons. It selects the LC-NE units with the criteria of the paper's code, tests the choice and engagement regressions, go-cue, engagement, switch and outcome coding of single neurons and of axons in prelimbic cortex, their relation to position in LC, and the pupil and lick analyses. The anatomy, transcriptomics and slice findings are not in the dandiset.
